_comment: One war told as a book of episodes (campaign.md in this folder's parent). Each season is one story folder, scouted, planned, written and finished like any episode; the book reads them in order. The seasons' `edge`, `pivotal` and `start` are LEADS, as in candidates.json: never facts and never a ranking. A scout establishes each from fetched sources and the edge re-check tries to refute it. The working title, subtitle and question are the author's to change.
title: Caesar in Gaul
subtitle: The war of 58 to 50 BC, from the record
author: Lawrence, 2026-10-28: "Yes go ahead and do this: turn Alesia into a book about Caesar's whole war in Gaul (58–50 BC)." The second telling of Alesia (alesia-52bc-2, accepted 2026-10-20, published 2026-10-21) is the book's climax.
question: How did Caesar take Gaul in eight years: his edge, luck, or a divided Gaul?
_question: The one question the whole book answers; each season's own question (plan.json) serves it. The scout's outline proposed it at 34 words; the author approved the idea, 2026-10-28: "This question is fine, but Way too wordy, please put questions like this in my voice". So it is one short line, and every season's question is too (thresholds `plan.questionMaxWords`).

commentaries.source: Caesar, The Gallic Wars, McDevitte & Bohn translation (Project Gutenberg 10657, the same text alesia-52bc-2 quotes as its main account)
commentaries.note: Caesar wrote one book per year, I to VII (58 to 52 BC); Aulus Hirtius wrote the eighth (51 to 50 BC). Each season's own-words span is its year's book.

seasons.subject: Caesar in Gaul, 58 BC: the Helvetii and Ariovistus
seasons.edge: Roman works and discipline: a wall and trench along the Rhone that turned a whole people's migration back; a bridge thrown over the Arar in a day; javelins that pinned shields together at Bibracte; a reserve line sent in at the decisive moment against Ariovistus
seasons.pivotal: Caesar's first season: a migration and a German king's claim became the reason for a Roman army to stay in Gaul
start: gutenberg: Caesar, The Gallic Wars, Book I
lacus-curtius: Cassius Dio, book 38; Plutarch, Life of Caesar
internet-archive: Napoleon III, History of Julius Caesar, vol. 2 (1866 English edition)
wikipedia: Battle of Bibracte; Battle of Vosges (58 BC) (leads and references only)

seasons.subject: Caesar in Gaul, 57 BC: the Belgae and the battle on the Sabis
seasons.edge: Training: legions caught unready on the Sabis formed and fought without orders; a fortified camp; a siege tower whose movement made a hill town give in
seasons.pivotal: The Belgae, whom Caesar calls the bravest of the Gauls, were broken; Rome's thanksgiving for the year was the longest yet given
start: gutenberg: Caesar, The Gallic Wars, Book II
lacus-curtius: Cassius Dio, book 39; Plutarch, Life of Caesar
internet-archive: Napoleon III, History of Julius Caesar, vol. 2
wikipedia: Battle of the Sabis; Battle of the Axona (leads and references only)

seasons.subject: Caesar in Gaul, 56 BC: the Veneti at sea
seasons.edge: A sea fight against ships too high and too strong to ram, won by cutting their rigging with hooks on long poles, and by a calm
seasons.pivotal: The Atlantic coast and its sea trade with Britain passed to Rome; the Veneti's fate was a warning to the other peoples
start: gutenberg: Caesar, The Gallic Wars, Book III
lacus-curtius: Cassius Dio, book 39; Strabo, Geography, book 4 (the Veneti and their ships)
internet-archive: Napoleon III, History of Julius Caesar, vol. 2
wikipedia: Battle of Morbihan (leads and references only)

seasons.subject: Caesar in Gaul, 55 BC: the Rhine bridge and Britain
seasons.edge: A timber bridge over the Rhine built in days, as a demonstration; a landing in Britain against chariots and a shore Rome did not know, where the tide wrecked the ships
seasons.pivotal: The first Roman army across the Rhine and in Britain. At Rome the slaughter of the Usipetes and Tencteri was debated: Cato is reported to have proposed handing Caesar over to the Germans
start: gutenberg: Caesar, The Gallic Wars, Book IV
lacus-curtius: Plutarch, Life of Caesar and Life of Cato the Younger; Cassius Dio, book 39; Suetonius, Life of Julius Caesar
internet-archive: Napoleon III, History of Julius Caesar, vol. 2
wikipedia: Caesar's Rhine bridges; Julius Caesar's invasions of Britain (leads and references only)

seasons.subject: Caesar in Gaul, 54 BC: Britain again, and the winter of the ambush
seasons.edge: In Britain, chariots against legions; in Gaul, Ambiorix's deception drew a legion and a half out of its camp to be destroyed, and the Nervii besieged Quintus Cicero with Roman-style works learned from prisoners
seasons.pivotal: The first Roman disaster in Gaul, which set off the risings of the next two years
start: gutenberg: Caesar, The Gallic Wars, Book V
lacus-curtius: Cassius Dio, book 40; Plutarch, Life of Caesar; Suetonius, Life of Julius Caesar
gutenberg or wikisource: Cicero, letters to his brother Quintus, 54 BC (an old translation; Quintus served in Britain and held the camp the Nervii besieged)
wikipedia: Battle of Atuatuca (leads and references only)

seasons.subject: Caesar in Gaul, 53 BC: the hunt for Ambiorix
seasons.edge: A second Rhine bridge; Caesar's choice to let the Eburones' neighbours plunder their country for him; a German raid that nearly took the camp at Aduatuca
seasons.pivotal: The Eburones were destroyed and a Carnute leader was put to death, which the next year's rising answered
seasons.doubt: The edge test may fail for this season. If the re-check fails it, do not drop it: propose to the author either a short season or folding it into its neighbour, 54 BC or 52 BC.
start: gutenberg: Caesar, The Gallic Wars, Book VI
lacus-curtius: Cassius Dio, book 40
internet-archive: Napoleon III, History of Julius Caesar, vol. 2

seasons.subject: Caesar in Gaul, 52 BC: Vercingetorix's rising, from Cenabum to Gergovia
seasons.commentaries: Book VII, from its opening to the cavalry battle before Alesia
seasons.edge: Vercingetorix turned Rome's supply against it by burning his own people's towns; Roman siege works took Avaricum against Gallic counter-mining; at Gergovia the edge failed when the legions did not hear or heed the recall
seasons.pivotal: For the first time Gaul fought under one commander; Caesar's defeat at Gergovia and the Aedui's defection led to Alesia
seasons.ends: Where alesia-52bc-2's own-words span begins: "All his cavalry being routed, Vercingetorix led back his troops". That telling's chapter 1 sums up this season in 1,500 words; the book build decides how the two meet (campaign.md §5).

lacus-curtius: Cassius Dio, book 40; Plutarch, Life of Caesar
internet-archive: Napoleon III, History of Julius Caesar, vol. 2
wikipedia: Siege of Avaricum; Battle of Gergovia (leads and references only)

seasons.subject: The Siege of Alesia
seasons._landed: Written, accepted by the author (2026-10-20) and published (2026-10-21). Not scouted again. Its dossier's people and peoples are the cast lines the other seasons reuse (campaign.md §3).

seasons.subject: Caesar in Gaul, 51–50 BC: Uxellodunum and the end of the war
seasons.edge: A hill town held out until its water was cut: archers on the stream, then a mine driven to the spring
seasons.pivotal: The last organised resistance in Gaul ended; what Rome did to the defenders was meant as a warning
start: gutenberg: Caesar, The Gallic Wars, Book VIII (Hirtius), in the same text
lacus-curtius: Cassius Dio, book 40
internet-archive: Napoleon III, History of Julius Caesar, vol. 2 (on where Uxellodunum was)
wikipedia: Siege of Uxellodunum (leads and references only)

decisions._comment: The author's answers to the outline (AI Write 9901D04D), 2026-10-28. Each binds the season it names.
decisions.question: Approved, made short (above).
decisions.gaul-53bc: A short season of 4 to 5 chapters, not folded into 54 BC. ("yes that is fine")
decisions.gaul-51bc: Frontinus (s5) does not count as an independent source: it names 'the city of the Cadurci', never Uxellodunum. The season is tier C, about 2 chapters. ("thats fine")
decisions.warsEnd: The war's end (what came after 50 BC) is told in gaul-51bc's afterword. ("thats fine")
decisions.recheck: The edge re-checks of gaul-54bc, gaul-53bc, gaul-52bc-rising and gaul-51bc ran on Sonnet; they run again on the strongest model before those seasons are planned. ("yes that is fine")
decisions.audiobook: When every season has landed: "please give me an audio book of the entire thing from my local Ollama Easton TTS voice: English-only Easton audiobooks", and "It should just be published under audiobooks" so he can play it on his iPhone.
decisions.pace: Seasons are written one after another without stopping for his read between them: "Once everything is done please give me an audio book of the entire thing".
